prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability is already established by court order, so the jury trial will turn entirely on (1) the date of taking and (2) which expert valuation the jury credits. HRT's strongest, most defensible number is its own appraiser's $3,008,000 (tied to the January 1, 2009 date HRT is arguing for), against the City's low-end $1.5 million (tied to its preferred 2010/later date); the owner's $5 million and the disavowed $6 million placeholder are outlier figures unlikely to control. A recovery in the $2-3.3 million range, plus a likely post-judgment § 1988 fee award, is the most probable outcome.

outcome.description: The first jury fixed the taking date at January 1, 2009 and awarded $4.25 million; the district court ordered a remittitur to $2,008,000, the City rejected it, and a second jury awarded HRT $1,976,820 in just compensation. The Sixth Circuit affirmed on December 22, 2025 (ripeness, res judicata, liability, bifurcation and the remittitur all upheld; Thapar, J., dissenting on res judicata). Amount used is the operative second verdict.
outcome.finalNote: Affirmed; the operative judgment is the second jury's $1,976,820 (first verdict of $4.25 million was remitted and retried).
